standard.title: Investigate drama across cultures and contexts
standard.description: investigate ways the elements of drama and/or conventions are used to communicate ideas, perspectives and/or meaning in drama created and/or performed across cultures, times, places and/or other contexts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can identify how elements of drama and conventions communicate ideas (AC9ADR6E01). They have not yet investigated how cultural, historical and contextual factors shape these choices across diverse dramatic traditions.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students investigate how elements of drama and conventions communicate ideas, perspectives and meaning across cultures, times and contexts.

nodes.label: Identifying elements and conventions in drama works
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify specific elements of drama and conventions in a given work and describe how each contributes to meaning
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two elements of drama or conventions in a given work; describe how each contributes to the meaning or effect
nodes.typical_width: Analyse a range of drama works to identify elements and conventions; explain how specific choices communicate intended ideas or perspectives
wider: Use Viewpoints questions to analyse a drama — 'What ideas did the drama express?', 'What conventions established time/place/context?', 'How was movement used?' — evaluate what each question reveals
Write or record a review of a drama focusing on specific elements and conventions — evaluate how each element choice communicates or fails to communicate intended ideas
Compare how the same element of drama (e.g. tension, symbol) is used in works from different genres or cultural contexts — analyse what the comparison reveals

response_modes.reason: Students need to accumulate experience with a range of drama works and the elements and conventions used within them before they can reason about how context shapes choices. A single example gives too narrow a lens for genuine comparative analysis across cultures and times.

success_criteria: Identifies at least two elements or conventions in a given work
Describes how each contributes to meaning — not just names the element
Does not confuse describing what happens in a drama with explaining how it communicates

nodes.label: Investigating context and meaning
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can investigate how cultural, historical and contextual factors shape how elements and conventions communicate ideas and meaning in drama
nodes.minimum_width: Investigate one drama work whose choices are shaped by cultural or historical context; explain how context influences specific element or convention choices
nodes.typical_width: Investigate drama works across at least two different cultural or historical contexts; analyse how context shapes choices and explain how the same conventions communicate differently across contexts
wider: Investigate how the impact of time and place shapes dramatic meaning — analyse how a drama from a historical period communicates differently to contemporary audiences
Analyse how linear and non-linear narrative is used in drama from diverse cultures — compare what each narrative structure produces for an audience
Investigate drama from a country or region in Asia — analyse how the cultural context shapes element and convention choices in ways that differ from Australian or European drama traditions

response_modes.reason: Students commonly describe what a drama does without connecting it to the cultural or historical context that shaped the choices. Investigating works from multiple distinct cultural and historical contexts — Asian drama traditions, historical periods, contemporary diverse contexts — forces students to develop the contextual reasoning habit rather than applying one familiar analytical frame.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The historical reception direction — how a drama communicates differently to contemporary vs original audiences — opens genuinely rich analytical territory about how meaning is not fixed in a text but constructed in context. Advancing students who investigate this develop a more sophisticated understanding of how drama works as a cultural practice.
success_criteria: Investigates at least one work whose choices are connected to cultural or historical context
Explains how context influences specific element or convention choices
Goes beyond surface description to explain the relationship between context and meaning

nodes.label: Connecting investigation to own drama practice
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use investigation of drama across contexts to inform specific decisions in own devising, interpreting or performing
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one insight from investigating other drama works that has influenced a decision in own practice; explain the connection
nodes.typical_width: Analyse how investigating drama across contexts informs own choices about elements, conventions and dramatic action; document specific influences and how they are adapted rather than imitated
wider: Develop a journal documenting how investigation of diverse drama traditions has opened new possibilities in own practice
Investigate how drama from other cultural traditions uses specific conventions — experiment with how those conventions might inform own devising without cultural appropriation
Construct an argument about why investigating diverse drama traditions produces stronger and more distinctive own practice than drawing on a single tradition

response_modes.reason: This node requires students to bring together element/convention analysis (Node 1) and contextual investigation (Node 2) and connect both to own practice decisions. Students who can analyse other works but cannot use that analysis to inform own drama have not met the standard's full investigative demand.

Students commonly describe what they have investigated without articulating how it changes specific decisions in own work. Scaffolding the connection — what did I learn, what decision did it change, how is my adaptation different from imitation — builds the analytical-to-practical transfer.

success_criteria: Identifies at least one insight from investigating other works that influenced own practice
Explains the connection — not just 'I was inspired by'
Distinguishes informed adaptation from imitation or appropriation
